propositions: Nested pytest child process launched without private --basetemp joins shared user-global numbered temp root, causing pytest session shutdown to synchronously scan and delete unrelated retained trees that can consume the 90-second timeout after test success.

Controlled filesystem A/B test with 400,000 stale entries in shared root vs private basetemp demonstrates cleanup cost scales with retained entries (10.8s vs 0.882s), and SIGUSR1 capture confirms main thread stalled in shutil._rmtree_safe_fd during post-100% pytest cleanup.

Nested pytest helper contract requires selected test completion within bounded child run while ambient tracker HEAD/directories remain unchanged; unrelated global temp cleanup working consuming that timeout violates isolation invariant.

Fix adds caller-owned tmp_path/nested-pytest private basetemp via --basetemp argument to nested child invocation, isolating cleanup without changing selection, environment, timeout, capture, or ambient-store assertions.

Regression oracle detects if nested pytest deletes another run's temp tree sentinel; mutation test confirms oracle is RED before fix, GREEN after fix, and RED again under omitted-basetemp, then GREEN on restoration.
25 repeated stress runs of extras-enforced full suite completed without timeout after fix; nested runs exhibit consistent 0.579–0.972s timing with poisoned shared root unchanged.
